title: Inflight signal debouncer and soft-fail autorepair
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Control plane: add inflight health-signal debouncer and soft-fail autorepair. Improves regional stability by reducing transient circuit flips and automating warmup of replacement nodes. Backwards compatible; rollout behind feature flag.
description: Context: Recent incidents (SUP-1245) revealed that short-lived probe flapping and transient KV-cache drain notifications cause cascading circuit transitions and aggressive tenant evictions during regional hiccups. This causes unnecessary soft-fail handoffs and customer-visible latency spikes. Motivation: reduce sensitivity to short-lived signals while retaining fast detection for real degraded nodes. Approach: introduce an "inflight signal debouncer" in the control plane health aggregator plus a complementary "soft-fail autorepair" that can warm standby capacity and pre-warm KV caches when a node shows ephemeral badness. The PR contains: - Debouncer: aggregates node-level signals (probe success/fail, drain markers, connection errors) on an event timeline, applies configurable hysteresis, and emits a single debounced health state change only after observation windows and weighted votes. - Soft-fail autorepair: when a debounced soft-fail is detected (transient but repeated within a short epoch), the orchestrator creates a micro-warmup plan: pre-warm a spare replica, populate prefix cache for top-ten tenants for that node, and hold eviction decisions for a short cooldown to avoid oscillation. - Telemetry/observability: new metrics (controlplane.debounce.window_ms, controlplane.debounce.vote_count, controlplane.softfail.warmups, controlplane.softfail.cooldown_s), structured tracing events for debouncer decisions, and dashboard panels in SLO console for warmup success rate. - Safety: feature-flagged rollout (featureflags.inflight_debouncer) with an escape hatch that forces immediate legacy behavior. Includes rate limits on warmup operations to protect capacity. - Tests/benchmarks: unit tests for debouncer logic, integration test simulating flapping probes, and a small perf microbenchmark showing <1% avg latency added to control plane decision path under 5000 events/sec. Checklist: - [x] Debouncer core algorithm implemented and covered by unit tests - [x] Orchestrator integration and warmup plan plumbing - [x] Telemetry + dashboards instrumented - [x] Feature flag and rollout plan documented - [x] E2E integration test simulating SUP-1245 repro - [x] Load perf benchmark run and results attached Link: Linear ticket https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4312 "Debounce inflight health signals and soften soft-fail behavior". Notes on config: defaults tuned conservatively (window_ms=1000, vote_threshold=3, warmup_cooldown_s=120). Operators can tune in runtime config if needed. Migration and compatibility: API contract unchanged. Debouncer lives inside control plane aggregator; upstream consumers receive the same health state events but with less churn. Rollout strategy: staged in canary region -> 25% -> 50% -> global, with telemetry checks at each stage to ensure no increased mean-time-to-detect for true failures.
